_comment: Per-tenant opt-in config for enforce-journal-entry.py, a Stop hook. Copy to <trusted home>/.config/journal/journal-entry.json, where <trusted home> is the passwd/token home the OS resolves, never $HOME (#2310); set $JOURNAL_CONFIG_DIR to an absolute directory to place the config elsewhere, the one escape hatch for a tenant who cannot write under the passwd home. With no config (or enabled != true) the hook no-ops. When a session has done substantive work (a successful Edit/Write/MultiEdit outside the Journal, tmp roots, the scratchpad, and the auto-memory dir; or a successful Bash with a work command at command position) and no tool call in the session wrote to the Journal (a write under the journal dir resolved from .vardemem.json, a `vardemem put <date>` at command position, or a Bash that redirects or copies into the journal path; quoted spans and heredoc bodies are data), the hook BLOCKS the Stop once with a reason naming the journal dir, so the agent writes the entry before ending. max_blocks_per_session caps the blocks per session_id (default 1; 0 is observe mode: the verdict is logged to ~/.local/log/enforce-journal-entry-hook.log and the ledger under ~/.local/state/journal/, and nothing blocks). min_work_events is the work threshold. work_commands are plain prefixes, matched at command position of each shell segment (after env assignments and env/sudo/nice leaders); a segment carrying --dry-run or --help never counts, and a verb that is only mentioned (grep 'git commit', echo 'git push') never counts. ignore_path_segments are directory names whose writes never count as work. The journal path is never hardcoded: it is read from the `journal` key of the .vardemem.json found by walking up from the session cwd (trusted roots only, per ~/.config/vardemem/trust.json), then from $AGENT_VAULT. Disable by naming enforce-journal-entry in $JOURNAL_DISABLED (the legacy $HARNESS_MANAGEMENT_DISABLED is honored).
